headline: Sox cruise to big win as the playoff push continues
morning_brew: Finally, a night where we didn't have to watch the ninth inning through our fingers like it was a horror movie. Ranger Suarez was an absolute machine on the mound, carving through that Royals lineup for seven innings and giving our bullpen the night off from their usual arson squad antics. It is the kind of performance that reminds you why we are still in the thick of this wild card race, and honestly, seeing the team play with some actual urgency at Fenway felt like a cold breeze on a humid day.

The bats were clicking, too, with Nick Sogard and Wilyer Abreu coming through in the clutch to pad the lead. We have been looking for consistency for weeks, and when you can get ten hits and play clean baseball, you stop looking like a team that is just hoping to survive and start looking like one that actually belongs in October. I am not saying we are out of the woods, but depositing another win into the Duck Boat fund feels pretty damn good this morning.

We are back at it this afternoon for the series finale at the Fens, and if we can keep this momentum rolling against Kansas City, we will head out on our road trip with a lot more confidence. My neighbor Rick is still busy filing his latest umpire grievance at his kitchen table, but even he had to admit that the officiating didn't steal the show last night. Let's hope for a repeat performance today because every single win is a giant step toward keeping those postseason dreams alive.
